notes.pace: November referral onboardings stand at 339 through 26 full days, with 6 more so far today, running about 13.9 a day over the last week. Straight line that lands near 391 by month end; the day-weighted projection is about 415, in a 402 to 432 range. No target is set for November, so this is the projection only. Four days remain including today, and either way November lands below Aug (465), Sep (612) and Oct (676).
notes.daily: Campaign signups by week: 7 from 7 referrers in the week of 16 Nov, then 116 from 93 referrers (about 1.25 each) in the week of 23 Nov as the new ladder opened. The last full day, 26 Nov, drew 27 signups from 23 referrers, with 20 onboarded and 1 activation. No single referrer sent more than 25 signups in the last 24 hours.
notes.ladder: The live ladder is the November campaign: a gold coin at 1 activated referral, a Marshall speaker at 4, a Thailand trip at 10, one gift per referrer. 87 referrers are in, and 64 of them have a referee signed up but not yet activated. Two referrers have reached the gold coin rung and 85 sit one activation away from it; no one has reached the speaker or the trip yet, and nothing has been claimed. The busiest referrer has 15 signups and 10 onboarded but no activation yet.
notes.cohorts: Against October, activated exporters are referring at 1.08 percent this partial month versus 1.49, and the reading is down across almost every cohort. Never-referrers (1a) are at 0.69 percent, down from 0.95. Past referrers (1b) sit at 2.62 versus 3.59. The one group up is November's own new activations (2), referring at 4.11 percent versus 3.71, with not-yet-activated onboarders also edging up. What lift there is comes from fresh activations, not the existing base.
notes.mix: First-time referrers drove most of the volume: 53 of them sent 58 signups, about 1.09 each, 52 percent onboarded, 1 activated. Eight reactivated never-referrers sent 10 signups at 80 percent onboarded. Eighteen one-time repeat referrers sent 18 signups at 78 percent. The eight heaviest repeat referrers sent 23 signups, 2.88 each, 61 percent onboarded with 1 activation.
notes.weeklyQuality: The week of 23 Nov brought 109 signups, 56.9 percent onboarded within a day and 60.6 percent within a week, with a median of 1.4 days to onboard. Three percent of those onboarded have activated so far, which is normal this early.
notes.claims: No gift has been claimed on the live ladder yet. The first rung needs an activated referral, and only two referrers have reached it.
notes.popupHeader: The claim popup reached 5,161 unique exporters from 23 to 26 Nov. Mixpanel answered on this run, so these numbers are fresh.
popup: 5,161 exporters saw the referral widget between 23 and 26 Nov; 10 tapped the claim button and 10 confirmed a claim.
One exporter chose to keep referring rather than claim, so claim intent is turning into confirmed claims almost one for one.
referrers: 87 referrers sent 109 signups this campaign, 66 onboarded and 2 activated so far.
79 of them sent a single referral, 61 percent onboarded.
Eight sent more than one, 30 signups between them at 60 percent onboarded and no activation yet.
The top referrer sent 15 signups with 10 onboarded and none activated.
33 referrers have nothing onboarded yet, covering 35 signups.
12 referrers have never activated a transaction themselves, sending 15 signups with 4 onboarded and 1 activation.
refereeQuality: October referrals, 982 signed up, onboarded at 58 percent within a week; of the 623 now mature, 22.2 percent activated, with a median first transaction near 1,629 dollars.
November referees from single-signup referrers, 317 of them, onboarded at 58.7 percent; 16.7 percent of the mature ones activated, median first transaction about 2,831 dollars.
November referees from referrers who sent two or more, 198 of them, onboarded at 53.5 percent; 23.5 percent activated among the mature, median first transaction near 1,624 dollars.
By business type, freelancers are the largest share of referees at about 60 percent and activate near 16 percent, while companies are a small slice but activate highest at 30 percent.
By stated volume, exporters under 10K dollars a month are 60 percent of referees and activate near 18 percent, and the few stating 50K and above activate at 50 percent.
notes.qualityHeader: Referee quality refreshed 27 Nov, using an exchange rate of 94 rupees to the dollar.
notes.qualityWindow: Figures cover the October and November referral cohorts, with activation measured only on referees mature enough to have had time to transact.
notes.excluded: Excluded from every campaign number on this page: exporter 85276 (freelancer, onboarded May 2025, never transacted), who has sent 2,218 campaign signups since 23 Sep, 93 of them in the last seven days, with 31 onboarded and none activated. The first burst on 24 Sep came in at one signup every 56 seconds from distinct phone numbers, the pattern of a link posted into a large group rather than personal referrals. Flagged referrers like 85276 are left out of campaign metrics but their onboardings still count toward the monthly target. Exporter 272788 sent 1,067 signups between 18 and 24 Oct, 18 onboarded and none activated, and is flagged the same way: out of the campaign numbers, but its 18 October onboardings count toward the monthly target.
overview: November is partial. Referral signups are at 522 so far against 628 in August, 950 in September and 984 in October; onboardings are 345 and activations already 348, the last running ahead of every recent full month.
Share rate sits at 1.98 percent this month against 2.78 to 3.21 earlier, and the referral share of all onboardings is 14.7 percent, down from 19.7 in October but still above the summer.
The one thing to watch is share rate: activations look strong because the gold coin pulled transactions forward, but the rate at which the base actually refers has softened.
gold: The gold coin campaign stopped tagging new signups on 23 Nov, when the coin became the first rung of the November ladder; referees already tagged still earn it. Across its run it drew 494 signups from 378 referrers, 294 onboarded, 92 reaching a coin and 86 claimed, and 262 of the referrers were referring for the first time ever.

The pinned pilot is the frozen 16 Oct list of 10,060 never-referrers. Their weekly share rate ran about 0.43 percent in the nine weeks before the pin and rose to roughly 0.9 to 2.0 percent in the weeks after, off a small number of referrers each week.
First referrals came in slowly: a cluster around 5 to 11 days after the pin and a long tail stretching past three weeks. The numbers are small, so read them as direction rather than proof.
campaigns: The live November ladder has drawn 109 signups in 5 days, about 21.8 a day, onboarding 60.6 percent and activating 3 percent so far with no gifts claimed yet, still early. That pace sits below the Moonshot ladder's 29.6 a day but above most single-gift campaigns such as the Tommy bag at 17.2 and the power bank at 11.6.

The just-ended gold coin campaign ran at 12.7 signups a day over 39 days, onboarding 59.5 percent and activating 31.3 percent with 93.5 percent of earned coins claimed, in line with past gift campaigns on onboarding and claim rates.
month: On 26 full days, November projects to about 627 referral signups (597 to 666), 415 onboardings (402 to 432), 415 activations (402 to 437) and 169 gold coins. Signups and onboardings would land below October's 984 and 676, but activations above its 423 and coins far above the 9 it saw.

Now that the coin is open to everyone, referrals split fairly evenly: the pinned pilot group sent about 115 signups across 100 referrers while everyone else sent the bulk, and first-time and repeat referrers are close in number. Signups were tagged mostly to the gold coin (402) and the new ladder (109).
The coin pipeline has 205 referrers with a referee waiting to pay, covering 266 referees; at the assumed 0.52 baseline activation rate that points to roughly 303 eventual coins.
dailyRead: Yesterday, 26 Nov, the live campaign drew 27 signups from 23 referrers (12 first-timers), 19 onboarded, 8 activated and 3 coins, with 2,513 widget views. That is ahead of the same Thursday last week, which had 25 signups, 18 referrers and 11 onboarded.

Over the last seven days the campaign held steady: 149 signups against 136 the week before, 97 onboarded against 93 and 23 coins against 19, though activations eased to 52 from 57. The number to watch is activations, which trail signups by a week or two.
cohortGrid: In the latest full month, October, active never-referrers (1A) referred at 1.67 percent against a 1.90 percent average over the prior three months, down 0.23 points; new activations (2A) at 4.48 versus 4.27, up 0.21 points; active repeat referrers (1B) at 5.84 versus 5.34, up 0.5 points.

Month to date, measured on the first 26 days against the same days of the prior three months, never-referrers slipped: 1A overall 1.04 versus 1.63 (down 0.59 points), recent never-referrers (1A:new) 1.36 versus 1.99, and longer-tenure ones (1A:old) 0.67 versus 1.05. Repeat referrers (1B) also eased, 4.06 versus 4.81. The live offer is not moving never-referrers so far.
There are 375 referrers month to date against a full-October 569 and a prior-three-month average of 532. Every cohort shown is large enough to read.
